answer: Carve one spiral maze per applicant into the limestone floor of a karst grove, its turns seeded by the applicant's key, so no maze fits a second walker. The applicant walks it turn by turn, filing the chalk mark at each junction before the next gate opens; each mark chains to the last, so a copied path fails — no two grove floors share the same karst veins. A farm chasing 5,000 phantoms must carve 5,000 mazes: $1.45 million and 150,000 carving hours, because one floor holds one spiral and a walked maze never resets.
